extracted.intended_audience: media and communication scholars, journalism researchers, and cognitive psychologists studying news selection and newsworthiness (especially those interested in German research traditions)
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical and methodological analysis of 'news factors' (newsworthiness criteria) and how they operate both as selection criteria for journalists and as relevance cues guiding audience information processing and retention. Focuses on conceptualizations, empirical modifications, and measurement approaches in the German research tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: News factors as relevance indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors are conceptualized as relevance indicators that not only serve as selection criteria in journalism, but also guide information processing by the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate or operationalize news factors both in terms of their role in journalistic selection (what gets reported) and in terms of how they function as cues for audience attention, comprehension, and memory. Consider measures that capture both selection frequency and audience processing/retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptionalization: event characteristics vs. reality construction
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors can be conceived either as event characteristics or as characteristics of the reality construction by journalists and recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying or applying news factors, explicitly state whether factors are treated as intrinsic properties of events (e.g., proximity, impact) or as features emergent from journalistic framing and audience interpretation; this choice affects operationalization and interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic focus on media selection versus cognitive approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: For a long time scholars focused exclusively on news selection by the media; more recent approaches—inspired by cognitive psychology—conceptualize news factors as relevance indicators guiding audience processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should locate themselves on this spectrum: traditional content-selection studies versus cognitive-focused studies of how news cues affect perception and memory. Mixed approaches that link selection practices to audience cognition are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of news factors on media use and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors affect media use and the retention of news items; the article explores how and why these effects occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical evaluations should measure downstream audience outcomes (e.g., attention, recall, retention) in addition to selection; include causal or correlational tests of how specific factors increase media consumption or memory for items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications of assumed factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Various modifications of the assumed (traditional) news factors are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to adapt classical lists of news factors to context, medium (newspaper vs television), or empirical findings; explicitly justify any additions, removals, or redefinitions of factors in a given study or editorial policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological advancements in measurement of news factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The article presents methodological advancements in the measurement of news factors in selection processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use improved or varied measurement techniques (e.g., refined content-analytic coding schemes, experimental designs, audience-processing measures) and report reliability/validity. Describe how measurement choices capture selection mechanisms and cognitive effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of content analysis as a primary empirical tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Content analysis is a key method for studying news factors, as indicated by the article's keywords and focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When operationalizing news factors, employ systematic content-analytic procedures, clearly defined coding categories, and inter-coder reliability statistics; complement content analysis with audience measures where the research question concerns processing or retention.
